text: DAX intelligence for Power BI (design ready: docs/design-docs/dax-intelligence-design.md). Approved scope (operator 2026-07-05): (C1) safe hand-written DAX reference extractor in crates/powerbi-tmdl-parser (extract_dax_references producing columns/bracket_refs/functions; string+comment-aware lexer; stable seam for a future tree-sitter swap); (C2) DAX lint: Tier 1 syntactic via "engram verify <model.tmdl>" gate + Tier 2 semantic (broken/unqualified/qualified refs, measure cycles) via a new lint_dax MCP tool; add VerifyFinding.severity; (C3) extend impact_analysis to span Power BI nodes (resolve powerbi_node by name; traverse existing powerbi_edge BFS for column -> measure -> visual/report blast radius; additive powerbi_neighborhood + root_kind). Data-model: add PowerBiColumn.expression; emit pbi_uses_field measure->column/measure edges; new find_powerbi_nodes_by_name query. 6-phase plan: P1 extractor -> P2 carry column DAX -> P3 ref edges -> {P4 impact span, P5 lint tier1} -> P6 lint tier2+tool. No CozoDB schema change (powerbi_node/edge exist; BFS already traverses powerbi_edge). Supersedes tree-sitter-from-scratch (no grammar exists; see docs/decisions/2026-07-05-dax-parsing-approach-spike.md). Open Qs: lint_dax standalone vs unified; reuse pbi_uses_field vs new pbi_depends_on_measure; code<->PBI bridge deferred.

Full CLI <-> MCP parity: the MCP tool surface (src/tools/mod.rs dispatch) and the CLI command service (src/cli/commands/, src/bin/engram.rs) MUST mirror each other in functionality AND documentation, and ship a complete MCP-to-CLI command mapping doc. Current state (2026-07-05): substantial parity already exists and CLI --help annotates each subcommand with the MCP tool it mirrors (bind=set_workspace, daemon-status=get_daemon_status, workspace-status=get_workspace_status, flush=flush_state, sync=sync_workspace, index=index_workspace, search=unified_search, query-memory=query_memory, symbols=list_symbols, map-code=map_code, impact=impact_analysis, query-graph=query_graph, stats=get_workspace_statistics, health=get_health_report, branch-metrics=get_branch_metrics, report token-savings/eval/retry-metrics=get_token_savings_report/get_evaluation_report/get_mutable_script_retry_metrics). GAPS to close (MCP tools with no CLI subcommand): query_graph_neighborhood, create_task, update_task, query_changes (git-graph), index_git_history (git-graph), and the planned lint_dax (B0E2B374). Also verify reverse direction (every CLI subcommand maps to an MCP tool) and that verify/manifest local-only commands are documented as such. Deliverables: (1) close functional gaps so every agent-facing MCP tool has an equivalent engram <cmd> subcommand and vice versa (respecting daemon-vs-direct/local distinctions); (2) a canonical, maintained mapping doc (table: MCP tool | CLI command | daemon/local | notes) under docs/ and referenced from both surfaces; (3) doc parity: CLI subcommand help references its MCP tool (already a convention) AND MCP tool docs/catalog reference the CLI command; (4) a parity guard test/contract that fails when a new MCP tool is added without a CLI mapping (and vice versa) to prevent drift. Grounding: src/tools/mod.rs (dispatch + should_record_metrics), src/shim/tools_catalog.rs (compile-time catalog / manifest), src/cli/commands/*.rs, src/bin/engram.rs (subcommand help already annotates MCP names).

retrieval_eval graph metric: resolution_recall numerator (count_calls_edges, whole-graph) and denominator (call_sites, language-gated to config.languages) have inconsistent language scope. In multi-language workspaces indexed beyond config.languages (e.g. Rust+Python with default languages=[rust]), non-configured-language edges inflate the numerator so resolution_recall clamps to 1.0, hiding the real per-language recall. Fix: scope count_calls_edges to configured languages via join calls_edge->function_meta->file.language, OR count call_sites over all indexed languages. Source: 081-F Ship review (P2). Files: src/db/cozo_queries.rs count_calls_edges ~2397; src/tools/eval.rs count_workspace_call_sites ~72.

retrieval_eval resolution_recall unit mismatch (Copilot 081-F review C1): numerator count_calls_edges counts DISTINCT (from,to) calls_edge rows (edge is keyed by from,to per src/db/cozo_backend/schema.rs:321), while denominator count_workspace_call_sites counts EVERY parser occurrence. A function calling the same callee twice => denominator 2, numerator 1 => recall 0.5 despite both resolving. Fix needs edge multiplicity/provenance (persist call-site count per edge) OR dedupe denominator to (caller,callee) units before ratio. Relevant to 082-F gate accuracy. Files: src/db/cozo_queries.rs:2397; src/tools/eval.rs count_workspace_call_sites.

retrieval_eval graph regression tier does not exercise real path (Copilot 081-F review C7): tests/integration/retrieval_eval_regression_test.rs injects compute_graph_metrics(10,9,0) directly, bypassing parser inventory, edge persistence, count_calls_edges, count_dangling_calls_edges and the tool handler. The two graph-count defects (C1 multiplicity, C2 false-edge semantics) can regress while the committed baseline stays green. Follow-up: build/index a fixture workspace and assert graph metrics returned by the real run_retrieval_eval path.

retrieval_eval false_edge_rate only detects dangling callees, not incorrect-but-existing targets (Copilot 081-F review C2): count_dangling_calls_edges counts calls_edge whose 'to' is absent from function_meta. Because the indexer only creates an edge after the callee resolves to a function id (src/services/code_graph.rs:466), 'to' almost always exists => metric ~0. It cannot catch edges resolved to an ambiguous/incorrect existing definition, which is exactly what 082-F cross-file resolution must gate. Follow-up: retain parsed callee provenance and validate the chosen target (including ambiguity) to compute a true false-edge rate. Baseline doc now labels the current metric a conservative lower bound. Files: src/db/cozo_queries.rs:2409.

retrieval_eval denominator/index consistency (Copilot 081-F re-review 3563161256 + 3563161283): resolution_recall denominator (count_workspace_call_sites) is parsed from CURRENT working-tree files while the numerator (count_calls_edges) is read from the PERSISTED index. (a) Edits after indexing mix two revisions; the [0,1] clamp hides the mismatch. (b) Unreadable indexed files are silently skipped from the denominator while their stored edges remain in the numerator, inflating recall. Root cause shared with C1 multiplicity (stash 88B5FAFD): fix by persisting the call-site inventory at index generation (with a hash/generation match gate) instead of re-parsing disk at eval time. Files: src/tools/eval.rs count_workspace_call_sites ~64-99.

retrieval_eval semantic eval O(sample_size x symbols x log symbols) (Copilot 081-F re-review 3563161340): each sampled query calls hybrid_search which scores, clones, and fully sorts the entire candidate corpus before truncating to k, so k does not bound the work. Bounded by default sample_size=200 but impractical on very large repos. Follow-up: use a top-k heap/selection or a dedicated evaluator that avoids cloning+sorting all candidates per query. Files: src/services/retrieval_eval.rs evaluate_semantic ~199-215.

retrieval_eval semantic corpus completeness: all_functions query uses INNER JOIN against symbols/docstrings; symbols lacking a docstring row are excluded from the self-retrieval denominator. Consider LEFT JOIN + name-fallback query derivation so the corpus denominator reflects every indexed function, not only those with docstrings. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563208101 (081-F).

retrieval_eval graph evaluation memory bound: count_workspace_call_sites / graph eval accumulates every selected source file's contents into sources before parsing. Per-file size is capped but total workspace size is not, so an opt-in eval of a very large repo could duplicate the full source corpus in memory. Parse incrementally or in bounded batches. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563254111 (081-F).

Shared DB open reliability (U015-FLK1 residual): connect_db (src/db/cozo_backend/mod.rs) can surface a transient 'database is locked' (SQLITE_BUSY) on rapid sequential reopen of the same branch DB (Windows lock-release lag), because cozo 0.7.x unwraps internally. A bounded reopen-retry in connect_db fixes it durably but is OUTSIDE the 081-F plan freeze-scope, so it was reverted from PR#238 and a test-scoped retry used instead. Deliver as a separately-tested reliability change touching the shared DB open path. Related stash 100EACD8. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563254094.

get_workspace_status capability discovery atomicity: the status handler (src/tools/lifecycle.rs ~520) reads retrieval_eval_enabled from a config snapshot taken separately from the workspace snapshot (~469). A concurrent set_workspace updates workspace + config in separate awaits, so status could pair one workspace's path/branch with another config's retrieval_eval_enabled. Capture workspace+config atomically via snapshot_dispatch_context() at handler start (as tools/eval.rs does). Pre-existing pattern; 081-F only added one field. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563399174.

retrieval_eval retrieval-mode fidelity: evaluate_semantic cannot distinguish true hybrid retrieval from a silent keyword-only fallback. hybrid_search calls embed_text(query).ok(), so model-load/inference failures are discarded and the run is still persisted without recording the changed mode, making reports/thresholds incomparable across environments and letting exact-keyword matches mask a broken embedding path. Either propagate embedding failure for eval runs, or add an explicit retrieval-mode/fallback field and segregate baselines by mode. Related 4CF046A5/54848E3D. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563399193 (081-F).

retrieval_eval TSX language-gate inconsistency: language_for_gate (src/services/retrieval_eval.rs ~55) maps 'tsx' to 'typescript', but the indexer stores TSX under canonical id 'tsx' (code_graph.rs ~1359 / Language::as_str). So languages=['tsx'] includes TSX in the graph corpus but excludes every TSX function from semantic eval (and languages=['typescript'] does the reverse). Return 'tsx' so one canonical gate applies to both paths. Opt-in only (empty languages default gates all in). Related D6F70DCC. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563477451 (081-F).

retrieval_eval thresholds are inert at runtime: [retrieval_eval.thresholds] is a public config surface but run_retrieval_eval never consults parts.config.thresholds; check_thresholds is only invoked by the regression test tier against docs/eval/baseline.json. So setting thresholds has no effect on live 'engram eval' / run_retrieval_eval (a breached threshold still succeeds). Decide the contract: either enforce thresholds in the run/report + CLI exit code (mirroring engram verify), or document them as regression-tier-only and drop the live-config expectation. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comment 3563477424 (081-F).

Align authoritative retrieval-eval plan doc with delivered narrowed contract: docs/exec-plans/2026-07-10-engram-retrieval-eval-subsystem-plan.md still (line ~157) promises all-symbols + fully-qualified-name fallback whereas delivery evaluates functions only with bare-name fallback; and (line ~171) presents the broad false-edge-rate as the 082-F gate whereas the implemented query only detects dangling targets lacking a function_meta row (conservative lower bound, cannot flag ambiguous/mis-resolved existing targets). Update the plan so future 082-F acceptance work does not assume class/interface coverage, qualified-name uniqueness, or full false-edge detection. Related D07F0919/54848E3D. Source: Copilot PR#238 review comments 3563477455 + 3563477467 (081-F).

rec1 followup: qualification-aware and method-aware call resolution. Restore module-path, method receiver, and Type-associated call recall that findings 1 and 7 conservatively defer. Currently method calls and path-qualified calls are extracted with is_method and is_qualified markers but NOT promoted to calls_edge, to avoid false singleton edges. Design a resolver that matches Type::method and module::helper targets by their qualified index names so this recall is recovered without reintroducing false edges.

rec1 followup: persist and rehydrate staged_call rows through the JSONL dehydration path. Today staged_call rows are not exported, so after rehydration or a fresh upgrade the post-pass runs against empty staging and relies on preserved singleton edges. Carrying staged rows through JSONL would let the post-pass fully revalidate cross-file calls after a restart. This is Copilot finding 4 fuller suggestion.

rec1 followup Copilot finding 9: migrate-down calls-resolution lacks write exclusivity under a shared ENGRAM_DATA_DIR multi-daemon setup. DaemonLock is workspace-rooted but the resolved data dir can be shared across workspaces on the same branch, so another daemon can write the same CozoDB while the destructive migration retracts rows and drops the schema. Add an exclusivity mechanism keyed to the resolved database and held by all writers for the full migration, or reject shared external data directories for this command.

rec1 followup Copilot finding 10: the resolution-column schema rewrite in cozo_backend schema uses :replace but bypasses run_script_retrying. Under a concurrent open with a shared data dir the one-time upgrade can fail with SQLITE_BUSY and fail startup instead of retrying. Route the migration through the existing run_script_retrying helper for consistency with the rest of bootstrap.

rec1 followup optional: run the cross-file calls post-pass on the incremental sync path as well, not only full and force index. Today incremental sync stages new cross-file calls but does not resolve them until the next full index. Gated on performance; evaluate a scoped post-pass over only changed callers.

Carry-forward from remediation PR #243 (operator instruction 2026-07-11): add the merge-gate compound learning to docs/compound/ AND encode the rule in instructions. Draft content preserved in session files: .copilot/session-state/e571e150-14e3-4ff8-b6a0-6290b8c3c0c4/files/2026-07-11-merge-gate-compound-learning-draft.md -> commit as docs/compound/copilot-review-merge-gate-wait-for-head-review-2026-07-11.md. Also append the rule to .github/instructions/github-pr-automation.instructions.md section 1.2 (Completion signal) and reference it from the pr-lifecycle merge step. Rule: before merging, a Copilot review whose commit_id == current HEAD sha must have completed AND Copilot removed from requested_reviewers AND 0 unresolved threads AND mergeable_state==clean; re-check after EVERY push. Root cause: Copilot review is async and re-triggered by each push, so the window after the final push but before the new review lands transiently shows 0 unresolved + clean, letting comments post onto an already-merged PR (happened on #239 and #240; verified fixed on #243). Bundle into the next shipment.
